forecaster_note: New short to mid-period S swell mix will give us some waist to chest high surf at the south magnets around dawn. We should then see it pick up to about chest / head high through later AM through the middle of the day, before a slight easing later afternoon. Small for other breaks. Clean until mid-morning, then light onshores through middle of the day and some bump and crumble. Breezy NE'lies in the afternoon add lump to all but sheltered S facing spots. — Hugh McDowell, Surfline

wind.summary: Breezy NE onshore this afternoon, ~18 km/h gusting 28. Backs off to a light W offshore overnight, then NNW/W offshore all day Saturday.

shark.summary: No shark activity at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly in the last 24h. One SLS drone sighting up at Kiddies Corner, Palm Beach at 1:31pm today — 25km north, no impact on your spots. Feed is live (71 tagged detections statewide in 24h, newest 1.4h ago).

days.label: Today
days.note: Day's basically done — last light 6:04pm. It ran to plan: clean W/WNW until mid-morning, then NE onshore from midday turned it to bump. Long Reef and Curl Curl held the S swell best. Saturday is the next paddle.

dee-why.window: Window has closed — NE onshore since midday. Next clean window is Saturday dawn.
alerts: Primary swell is dead S (184°) — wraps flat into the Dee Why bowl

tip.label: Frontside read
tip.text: Today the S swell sat at 184° — dead south, folded flat into the bowl with no shape. Worth remembering: when the primary is 170–190°, skip the point and go to Long Reef instead.

long-reef.window: Window has closed — best of the day was 6–11am. Saturday holds the most size again.

tip.label: Pick of the day
tip.text: Straight-in S exposure meant Long Reef ate today's swell — 3–5ft versus Dee Why's 2–4ft. Same story Saturday and Sunday.

curl-curl.window: Window has closed — south corner held longest. Back at it Saturday.

tip.label: Backup
tip.text: South corner is the play on a dead-S swell — sheltered from the NE and still fed. Lefts here are your backside.

alerts: Too far north — S swell barely reaches

tip.label: Skip it
tip.text: Too far north for a dead-S swell. Only worth it if you're already in Manly.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The next real paddle. Swell drops back — energy halves to ~54 kJ — but NNW/W offshore blows all day so it's clean dawn to dark. Long Reef and Curl Curl hold waist-to-chest. Floaty-board day, mid-morning is fine for once.

dee-why.window: Anytime — clean all day, just small. Mid tide best.

long-reef.window: 8am–2pm — breezy offshore, holds the most size.

curl-curl.window: All day — offshore NNW keeps the banks tidy.

manly.window: Marginal — cross-shore NNW and barely any swell.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday small but clean all day. Sunday is the one — a new mid-period S pulse fills in, energy spiking to 484 kJ and Long Reef pushing 6ft. But the window shuts early: offshore until ~11am, then onshore lump for the arvo. Monday morning has another clean chest-to-head window ahead of a strong southerly change.

dee-why.window: Sunday 9–11:30am — swell fills in before the onshore arrives.

long-reef.window: Sunday late morning — biggest of the weekend, up to 6ft.
alerts: Sunday PM goes onshore — don't leave it late

curl-curl.window: Sunday 9am–noon — south corner as the pulse arrives.

manly.window: Sunday morning only — still the smallest of the four.
